_: THE ZONE CONTRACT. Nothing in this pack types a track width, a percentage or a breakpoint. Every box in every image is ASSIGNED BY THE RESOLVER from the contracts below and then measured back; a render that disagreed with its own contract fails the build. Widths are necessary but not sufficient: a candidate arrangement must also pass intrinsic-asset fidelity, vertical occupancy and dead-space ownership before it is used.

base._note: The app sets no root font-size, so 1rem = 16px. Text minimums and maxima are in rem because they are reading measures, not device measures.

gap._note: One gap between any two tracks, in every primitive. Also the dead-space tolerance.

prompt.role: the question. A compact reading rail.
prompt.note: A TRACK IS A POSITION. No fill, no border, no stretching to the sibling's height.

solution.role: the numbered reasoning and the answer that closes it.
solution.note: `max` is a hard allocation ceiling, not only a prose cap. A track is never given width its region cannot use — see deadSpace.

case.role: one complete case in a comparison — its own question, reasoning and answer, stacked.
case.note: Equal grow: repeated children are identical by construction, so a comparison cannot develop a favoured side.

interpretation.role: what the figure shows and why it agrees with the working.
interpretation.note: MAINTAINER RULING WANTED: you suggested a 45-55rem maximum; the app ships MX_INTERP_MAX = 620px (38.75rem). The pack uses 40rem.

synthesis.role: the same semantic region as `interpretation`, in its other placement.
synthesis.note: ONE REGION, ONE STYLING CONTRACT, TWO PLACEMENTS. Beside a shared visual it is the interpretation rail; with no visual to belong to it spans the content region after the composition. The JSON key names the placement.

answer.role: the closing band of the solution it belongs to.
answer.note: INHERITED GEOMETRY. No width of its own; begins at its owning solution's content origin and flows as text.

figure._: A FIGURE IS SIZED FIRST, FROM ITS OWN CONTRACT, AND THE TEXT RECEIVES THE REMAINDER. The resolver never asks how much width is left over for the graph; it asks what box this graph needs and then builds a composition from what remains. A figure track is never `1fr`.

engineFloor._note: MX_PLOT_MIN_W / MX_PLOT_MIN_H — the engine's own floor, below which minimumReadableBox may never fall.

figure._signature: For every plane the build derives a FigureLayoutSignature by asking the engine, not by computing an aspect: minimumReadableBox (the smallest box in which the engine still paints one x-unit and one y-unit the same length, floored at engineFloor), preferredBox (preferredFraction of the largest square-scale box), maximumUsefulBox (the largest box whose longer side reaches maxUsefulLongSide while scale stays equal), plus the painted px-per-unit at each. equalScaleRequired is true for a Cartesian plane unless the lesson authors scaleMode:'authored'.
figure._ruling: MAINTAINER RULING WANTED: your worked example stacked at 900px because the figure held its 612px preferred box. The pack instead lets a figure shrink WITHIN [minimumReadable .. preferred] before abandoning the split, which your own caveat permits ("unless 484 is independently within the figure's acceptable range"). Under the pack's rule your 900px case splits at 484 + 32 + 384. Say which you want; it is one comparison in the resolver.

gates._: A candidate arrangement must pass ALL of these. They are hard feasibility conditions, not aesthetic scores — otherwise the resolver goes on choosing arrangements that are legal and obviously bad.
gates.width: every region meets its minimum useful width
gates.fidelity: every intrinsic asset (plane, table, equation) keeps the size it actually requires; a figure is never squeezed to preserve a split

occupancy._note: occupancy = a track's content height / the row's height. The SHORTER track must reach this fraction. A one-line question beside a seven-step solution occupies ~17% of its row and is rejected at any width. MAINTAINER RULING WANTED: you suggested testing 50-60%; the pack uses 0.55 and prints every measured occupancy so the threshold can be argued from data.

deadSpace._note: Every substantial region of horizontal space a composition creates must belong to a semantic region. A track is therefore never allocated more width than its region can use: distribute by growth weight, clamp each track to [min, max], and redistribute the surplus to tracks still below their maximum. Only when every region is at its maximum does leftover width appear, and then it is a trailing page margin — never a hole between or inside regions. Unowned inline space above one gap fails the candidate.

gates.overflow: content that cannot be set at the assigned width (a wide equation, a wide table) is handled locally — its own scroll — and never changes the sibling track, the type size or the composition
gates.ordering: the semantic order of regions is identical in every state

repeat.note: ITEM COUNT HAS NO EFFECT ON GEOMETRY, and neither does item VARIATION: a repeat's children share ONE verdict and the strictest child decides it. Otherwise a gate that rejects row 2 alone would produce exactly the ragged, count-sensitive layout the primitive exists to prevent.
repeat.fallback: across becomes down; down's children all stack together

visualInterpretation.purpose: a figure and the text that reads it, as siblings with one top edge
visualInterpretation.note: The figure is assigned its box FIRST, from its own signature. The interpretation rail takes the remainder, capped at its maximum.

stack.purpose: the regions in semantic order, one inset, no divider, nothing centred
stack.note: THE SAFE FALLBACK, NOT A FAILURE. A layout engine should be willing to say: there is plenty of width, and this particular content pair still does not belong side by side.

extended.assembly: states; each state takes the primitive its own content needs

resolver: 1  Read the semantic composition from the JSON. Never infer it from content.
2  Determine the legal primitive arrangements for that composition.

3  Obtain a layout signature for every region — minimum, preferred, maximum, rendered height; for a figure, its minimumReadable / preferred / maximumUseful boxes. Derived at layout time from rendered content, never authored.
4  Build candidate arrangements, sizing intrinsic assets FIRST and giving text the remainder.
5  Reject any candidate violating region minimum width, figure fidelity, reading measure, vertical occupancy, dead-space ownership, overflow handling or semantic ordering.
6  Score the survivors on closeness to preferred size, compactness, balanced occupancy and alignment continuity.

surfaces._note: CONTENT REGION widths, not viewport widths. 1152 is a 1536px viewport with the navigation rail open; 382 is a 414px handset; 700 is chosen for being a width nobody designed for.
